chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Supplication repels the decree even after it has been firmly decided. So increase your supplications, for it is the key to every mercy and the achievement of every need. What is with God — Mighty and Majestic — cannot be attained except through supplication. And indeed, there is no door that is frequently knocked upon except that it is imminent that it shall be opened for its seeker.

key_terms.أُبرم إبراماً: Firmly and completely decided; strengthened with reinforcement
key_terms.الدعاء: Supplication (du'a) — invoking God through prayer and petition
key_terms.القضاء: The divine decree or ordained matter; the decreed fate
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Epithet of God meaning 'Mighty and Majestic' — common divine honorific
key_terms.مفتاح: Key — metaphor for that which grants access to something otherwise inaccessible

ai.seo_question: Can supplication change the divine decree according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches the extraordinary power of du'a (supplication), asserting it can actually reverse divine decrees — even those that have been firmly established. This teaching was offered to Abdullah ibn Sinan, a trusted companion, in the context of encouraging persistent prayer. The original audience understood 'qada' (decree) within the Shia theological framework where divine decrees can be conditional, and this hadith supports the doctrine that God's mercy responds to human supplication.
